claim: R6-03's residue in the base's one statement of the port. §7.7 item 1 (base l. 11946–11950): 'the port DIFFS the incoming dossier against the dossier facts the map already carries … writes one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13), dates it by §4.11's dating rungs (item 76) and emits its events'; §14 port item 4 (l. 19919–19920) says 'into one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13)'. Since round 6, an absorb whose week is not after the last epoch's writes no change for three things it finds changed: a late calamity, its F5 targets' records and a condition naming it. Their carried facts stay as they were, and the next absorb past that week carries them (§4.11 *The clock* (4), l. 8531; V08 §3.6 (3), (4), l. 1873–1876, 1927–1928; V08 §3.2, l. 1530–1531). R6-01 (2) (d) puts the base's summaries in each ruling's sweep. R6-03's sweep searched §7.7 item 10 and §14's port comments for a held list, but not item 1's 'one per changed element'. Read alone, item 1 writes a `DossierChange` for each of the three, and the ledger fold (`carried[key] = after`) would then carry them. A port builder follows §4.11 (4) and V08 §3.6 (3), which item 1 cites by '§4.11', so nothing built changes. §14 item 4's 'groups them by §4.11's cadence' carries the exception by citation; its 'one per changed element' does not.
required_change: Determinism, §7.7 item 1: 'writes one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13), dates it by §4.11's dating rungs (item 76)' → 'writes one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13) — none, in an absorb whose week is not after the last epoch's, for a late calamity, its F5 targets' records and a condition naming it, which the next absorb past that week carries (§4.11 *The clock* (4)) — dates it by §4.11's dating rungs (item 76)'. Second end, scope: §14 port item 4, 'into one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13)' → 'into one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13; none for what §4.11 *The clock* (4) leaves uncarried)'.
